## Key terms

{{< glossary homogeneous-coordinates translation-matrix transformation-matrix composite-transformation trs-matrix local-space world-space camera-space direction translation >}}

## 13.1 Why a 2 × 2 matrix cannot move a shape

- Every 2 × 2 matrix sends (0, 0) to (0, 0): it can scale and turn, but
  never move.
- **Homogeneous coordinates:** the point (x, y) becomes **(x, y, 1)**.
- Transformations then become 3 × 3 matrices; their last row is always
  (0, 0, 1).
- To read the point again, drop the last 1: (7, 3, 1) is (7, 3).

![A 3 × 3 matrix can move the origin.](images/homogeneous.png){width=92%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
A point needs w = 1, not 0. With w = 0 the move is lost.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Add the third coordinate"}
Write (4, −2), (0, 3) and (0, 0) in homogeneous coordinates. Then multiply
any 2 × 2 matrix by (0, 0). What do you always get?
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Three coordinates"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="(2, 1, 0)|(1, 2, 1)"}
How do you write the point (2, 1) in homogeneous coordinates?
:   (2, 1, 1)

Which 2D point is (7, 3, 1)?
:   (7, 3)

What does any 2 × 2 matrix do to (0, 0)?
:   it keeps it at (0, 0)

What is the last row of a 3 × 3 transformation matrix?
:   (0, 0, 1)
:::
:::

## 13.2 The translation matrix

- **T(tx, ty) = rows (1, 0, tx), (0, 1, ty), (0, 0, 1)**: the move is in the
  last column.
- T(5, 2) × (2, 1, 1) = (7, 3, 1): the same as (2, 1) + (5, 2).
- Undo it with T(−tx, −ty).

![The translation matrix T(tx, ty).](images/translate-matrix.png){width=92%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
tx and ty go into the last column, not the last row.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Build T(−3, 4)"}
Write T(−3, 4) and multiply it by (5, 1, 1). Check with an addition.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · The translation matrix"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="(4, −1, 1)|T(1, 4)"}
What is T(4, −1) × (2, 5, 1)?
:   (6, 4, 1)

Which matrix undoes T(4, −1)?
:   T(−4, 1)

Where is the move in T(tx, ty)?
:   in the last column

What is T(−3, 4) × (5, 1, 1)?
:   (2, 5, 1)
:::
:::

## 13.3 Scaling and rotation as 3 × 3 matrices

- Put the 2 × 2 matrix in the top-left corner; the last column and row are
  (0, 0, 1).
- S(2) = rows (2, 0, 0), (0, 2, 0), (0, 0, 1).
- R(90°) = rows (0, −1, 0), (1, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1).
- R(90°) × (2, 1, 1) = (−1, 2, 1).

![Scaling and rotation in 3 × 3.](images/scale-rotate-3x3.png){width=92%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
The bottom-right corner is always 1, never 0.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Two 3 × 3 matrices"}
Write S(3, 1) and R(180°) as 3 × 3 matrices and multiply each by (1, 2, 1).
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · Scale and turn in 3 × 3"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="(3, 2, 3)|(1, −2, 1)"}
What is S(3, 1) × (1, 2, 1)?
:   (3, 2, 1)

What is R(180°) × (1, 2, 1)?
:   (−1, −2, 1)

What is R(90°) × (2, 1, 1)?
:   (−1, 2, 1)

What does the last column (0, 0, 1) of S and R mean?
:   no move
:::
:::

## 13.4 One matrix: M = T × R × S

- The **TRS matrix** M = T × R × S: first scale, then rotate, then translate
  (read from right to left).
- S(2), R(90°), T(5, 1): **M = rows (0, −2, 5), (2, 0, 1), (0, 0, 1)**.
- M × (1, 0, 1) = (5, 3). Step by step: (2, 0), (0, 2), (5, 3).
- The order matters: for (1, 0), T(2, 0) × R(90°) gives (2, 1), but
  R(90°) × T(2, 0) gives (0, 3).

![M = T × R × S.](images/trs-chain.png){width=92%}

{{< sim file="sims/matrix-chain.html" poster="sims/matrix-chain.png" title="Matrix Chain: M = T × R × S" height="820" >}}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
In M = T × R × S, S acts first, although it is written last.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Build M in Matrix Chain"}
Set scale 2, θ = 90°, tx = 5, ty = 1 and compare M with the notes. Then set
θ = 180°. Where does the nose (2, 0.3) go?
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 4 · The TRS matrix"}
M = T(5, 1) × R(90°) × S(2) = rows (0, −2, 5), (2, 0, 1), (0, 0, 1). Choose
the right answer.

::: {.match extra="(2, 5)|T first"}
Where does M send the point (1, 0)?
:   (5, 3)

Where does M send the point (0, 1)?
:   (3, 1)

Which matrix acts first in T × R × S?
:   S

What does R(90°) × T(2, 0) do to (1, 0)?
:   (0, 3)
:::
:::

## 13.5 Points and directions

- A **point** has w = 1: the move is added. A **direction** has w = 0: the
  move is multiplied by 0.
- M = T(5, 1) × R(90°): the point (1, 1, 1) goes to (4, 2, 1); the direction
  (2, 0, 0) only turns to (0, 2, 0).
- Unity: `m.MultiplyPoint3x4(p)` (w = 1) and `m.MultiplyVector(d)` (w = 0);
  `Matrix4x4.TRS(position, rotation, scale)` builds M.

![A point moves; a direction only turns.](images/point-direction.png){width=92%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
A velocity "moved" with the object flies the wrong way. Directions get
w = 0.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Point or direction?"}
With M = T(5, 1) × R(90°), apply M to the point (2, 0, 1) and to the
direction (2, 0, 0). Which one moved?
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 5 · w = 1 or w = 0"}
M = T(5, 1) × R(90°) = rows (0, −1, 5), (1, 0, 1), (0, 0, 1). Choose the
right answer.

::: {.match extra="(7, 1, 0)|w = 2"}
Where does M send the point (2, 0, 1)?
:   (5, 3, 1)

Where does M send the direction (2, 0, 0)?
:   (0, 2, 0)

Where does M send the direction (0, 3, 0)?
:   (−3, 0, 0)

Which w does a direction have?
:   w = 0
:::
:::

## 13.6 Local, world and camera space

- **Local space:** measured on the object. **World space:** in the level.
  **Camera space:** measured from the camera.
- The object's matrix M takes local to world; the inverse of the camera's
  matrix takes world to camera.
- Cannon (2, 1) on a ship at (10, 4), turned 90°: world (9, 6). Camera at
  (8, 3): camera space (1, 3).
- Unity: `transform.TransformPoint(p)` (local → world),
  `transform.InverseTransformPoint(p)` (world → local).

![Local, world and camera space.](images/spaces.png){width=92%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Camera space subtracts the camera position; it does not add it.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Three spaces"}
A ship at (6, 3), not turned, has a flag at (1, 2). The camera stands at
(5, 0). Where is the flag in the world, and in camera space?
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 6 · Three spaces"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="(5, 1)|(13, 5)"}
A ship at (6, 3), not turned, has a flag at (1, 2). Where is the flag in the world?
:   (7, 5)

The camera stands at (5, 0). Where is the world point (7, 5) in camera space?
:   (2, 5)

The same ship is turned by 90°. Where is the flag (1, 2) now?
:   (4, 4)

Which space measures from the object's own pivot?
:   local space
:::
:::

## Game challenge: Cannon Cove {.challenge}

Work alone. Use every section of today.

**Cannon Cove** is a pirate game. The cannon sits at **(2, 1)** in the
ship's local space. The ship enters the harbour at **(10, 4)**; later it
turns by **90°**. The camera stands at **(8, 3)**.

{{< sim file="sims/cannon-cove.html" poster="sims/cannon-cove.png" title="Cannon Cove: local, world and camera space" kind="game" height="760" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 7 · The cannon"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="(2, 1)|(17, 9)"}
The ship is not turned. Where is the cannon in the world?
:   (12, 5)

The ship is turned by 90°. Where is the cannon in the world?
:   (9, 6)

Where is the cannon (9, 6) in camera space?
:   (1, 3)

The cannon fires along local (1, 0). Which way does it fire on the turned ship?
:   (0, 1)
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 8 · New orders (harder)"}
Local cannon (2, 1), ship at (10, 4). Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="(12, 5)|(10, 4)"}
Which matrix puts the ship turned by 90° into the world?
:   rows (0, −1, 10), (1, 0, 4), (0, 0, 1)

The ship turns by 180°. Where is the cannon?
:   (8, 3)

The ship turns by −90°. Where is the cannon?
:   (11, 2)

The ship is turned by 180°. Where is the cannon in camera space (camera at (8, 3))?
:   (0, 0)
:::
:::

## Summary {.summary}

- Homogeneous coordinates: (x, y) becomes (x, y, 1); transformations become
  3 × 3 matrices.
- T(tx, ty) has the move in its last column; S and R have the 2 × 2 matrix
  in the top-left corner.
- M = T × R × S scales, then rotates, then translates, in one matrix.
- Points have w = 1 and move; directions have w = 0 and only turn.
- Local → world with the object's matrix; world → camera with the inverse of
  the camera's matrix.
